answer: Rate-limit identity admission with a verifiable delay function instead of price. A single serial VDF chain mints one new slot per fixed tick, say every ten minutes, and no capital can parallelize it: the chain must be walked one step at a time. A farm wanting a thousand clones needs a thousand ticks, roughly seven days, and every entry sits in a public atlas of the queue where a raven-like watcher flags burst registrations. An honest agent needs one island of identity, while an attacker hits a wall of elapsed time instead of a wallet it can drain.
